STEP 1 - Scene: A small side dish of roasted sweet potato (orange cubes with caramelized, slightly charred edges) on a white square plate. Photographed from above at a near-overhead angle, on a glass surface.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square plate is about 20 cm across (side plate size). Area ≈ 20 x 20 ≈ 400 cm^2 for the square outline, roughly 314 cm^2 if treated as a circle; I use ~350 cm^2 as the working area.

STEP 3 - Items: Roasted sweet potato cubes (about 8-10 pieces, some with dark caramelized skin), a few small crumbs or bits of a light-colored garnish (possibly a little cheese or breadcrumb residue), and a faint glaze/oil sheen.

STEP 4 - Area: Sweet potato pieces cover roughly 12% of the plate (about 42 cm^2). Crumbs and residue about 1% (3 cm^2). Total food coverage is about 13% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: Sweet potato pile 42 cm^2 x ~2 cm average height ≈ 84 ml gross volume. Crumbs/residue negligible (~3 ml).

STEP 6 - Grams: Sweet potato 84 ml x 0.6 g/ml ≈ 50 g. Crumbs ~2 g. Glaze/oil sheen ~2 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Roasted sweet potato ≈ 90 kcal/100 g, so 50 g ≈ 45 kcal. Crumbs (assumed cheese/breadcrumb-like) 2 g at ~400 kcal/100 g ≈ 8 kcal. Oil/glaze 2 g at 880 kcal/100 g ≈ 18 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 50-55 g of roasted sweet potato with a little glaze is plausible for a small side portion with only a few pieces visible. Total ≈ 55 g, ≈ 70 kcal.
